subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single TypeScript module for a corporate riot-control interceptor vehicle, thinking through its design as a heavy multi-wheeled armored truck with a roof-mounted water cannon turret and neon lighting, while keeping the output manageable in length.

I'm working through the skeleton structure, with wheel joints, turret yaw, cannon pitch, and ram plow elements, then figuring out how to build the hull body using lofted sections and extruded side profiles for the panelled, painted silhouette.

Now I'm planning the paint scheme: a dark navy-gray body with panel lines and yellow hazard stripes, countershaded with a corporate white-gunmetal livery accented by magenta and cyan stripes, using procedural paint functions keyed to vertical position.

For textures, I'm sketching out the decals: an invented corp logo ("VANTAGE SECURITY/VSEC" hexagon-V mark), a door label reading "RIOT SUPPRESSION UNIT 07," hazard stripe textures for the bumper, a glowing "DISPERSE" warning screen for the dashboard/rear display, a scrolling LED marquee reading "DISPERSE // NCPD COMPLIANT," and a reflective windscreen visor with HUD-style gradient streaks.

I'm also planning flank unit numbering, a water tank level gauge, flat-color glow for the light-bar lens, wheel hub detailing, and a mesh grille texture for the front intake, importing a glow kit for emissive parts.

Now I'm laying out the vehicle dimensions in meters -- roughly 6.4m long, 2.5m wide, facing +Z -- and working out where to place the three axle pairs for a 6x6 configuration, settling on roughly even spacing at z = 2.1, 0, and -2.1.

I'm refining the wheel and body widths so the tires peek out slightly beyond the hull for an armored-truck look, landing on a body half-width around 1.1m and wheel centers near ±1.12m, giving an overall width of about 2.7m. Then I'm setting the vertical layout -- 0.5m ground clearance, body bottom at 0.55m, cab roof around 2.3m, with a water cannon turret mounted higher on the roof or rear tank deck -- and planning a forward cab section paired with a boxy rear tank housing.

Now I'm sketching out the side profile as a sequence of (z,y) coordinates tracing the hull outline from front bumper through the sloped hood, raked windscreen, cab roof, and back into the rear tank body, adjusting heights like cab roof at 2.4 and rear body topping near 2.5-2.6 to fit the cylindrical tank and turret mount.

I realize cutting wheel arches directly into this extruded outline would create slots straight through the hull's width, which doesn't work for a single extrusion. Instead I'll keep the hull bottom flat and add separate fender/mudguard pieces as angled boxes over each wheel position in a darker color.

Working through the overall proportions now: with a turret the total height lands around 3.2m, which matches typical riot truck scale, and I'm positioning the turret ring at the rear body's top (y=2.6) with yaw/pitch joints stacked above so the cannon barrel clears the cab roof when pointing forward.

I'm plotting the side-profile outline points for the vehicle hull, tracing from the front bottom edge up over the nose, across the raised cab and rear body sections, and back down to close the loop, then setting up the extrusion along the x-axis.

For the hull surface shading, I'm designing a paint function that gives it a darker, grimier skirt near the bottom, a brighter white upper body, and a magenta neon stripe along the sides, with noise-based grime concentrated below y~1.0. I'm also wrapping this in a panelled() layer to add rivet-textured seams on top of the base livery.

Writing livery paint colors...

Still defining the darkened boundary gradient, adding a yellow accent band and grime noise near the roofline...

Now I'm picking the cyberpunk palette—cyan, magenta, yellow, red—and planning the light bars: alternating cyan/magenta on the roof, cyan underglow strips on the skirts, plus rear and grille bars with strong glow strength.

I'm sketching helper functions for building boxes and cylinders, a part wrapper, and a neon glow helper, then mirroring them for symmetric sides. For the skeleton, I'm setting the chassis root and planning wheel joints, including steering joints for the front wheels.

Naming the six wheels, I decide to aim each wheel joint's local axis outward along the axle rather than vertically, so rotating about that axis correctly spins the wheel instead of producing the wrong rotation direction seen in the sampler.

For the front wheels I'm adding separate steer joints at the hub position with a vertical axis, parented to the chassis, then nesting the wheel joint underneath for steering plus spin. For the turret I'm setting up a yaw joint at the base with a vertical axis and a pitch joint further up parented to yaw, aligning its bone along the barrel so it hinges correctly about the horizontal axis.

Now I'm thinking about adding door hinge joints on the cab sides, with the door positioned as a thin overlay panel slightly outside the hull surface, hinged at the front edge about a vertical axis, and including window glass and handle details sized to match the cab's windscreen and roofline geometry.

Working out the windscreen's tilt angle and dimensions to place a raked glass panel box matching the hull's sloped profile...

I'm positioning the center at the midpoint coordinates, then offsetting slightly along the outward normal direction (computed from the up-and-forward tilt) to place the surface correctly.

I'm sizing the windscreen plane at roughly 1.9 by 0.95, oriented so its face normal points outward along that same direction, and planning to apply a dark glass-style texture to it.

Now I'm thinking through the front hull details: a grille box with a mesh-pattern texture, plus thin cyan-white neon slits for headlights, positioned along the sloped front face.

I'm adding a heavy angled push bumper with hazard-stripe texturing, a wire guard over the lights, and a glowing roof light bar with alternating cyan and magenta lens segments plus end caps, along with rotating beacon joints on the cab roof corners.

I'm planning a rear light bar with a magenta/cyan wrap, cyan running strips along the lower hull, a magenta underglow box beneath the body, and a decal system for flank logos and "VANTAGE SECURITY // CROWD CONTROL" branding on the hull surfaces.

Thinking through the decal projection for the side logo, I realize glow should work fine on a decal part, so I can make the neon sign text itself glow against a transparent backing. The tricky part is handling mirroring for the opposite flank so the lettering reads correctly from both sides rather than appearing backwards.

I'm uncertain whether the u-direction convention could introduce mirroring issues for side decals, but given the ambiguity I'll just proceed without applying a mirror flag.

Working through the local axis math for each facing direction, computing the cross product of up and forward to determine the plane's local right-vector, and confirming it matches the viewer's expected orientation across different dir cases.

I'm deciding to use flat planes rather than decals for the flank logos since the hull sides are flat faces, offsetting the plane slightly from the surface to avoid z-fighting, and defining a helper function to place these flank textures. I'm also figuring out how glow should behave on textured parts — strokes in a neon-style texture with transparent background should glow while the dark background stays unlit.

Now I'm sketching out the texture list: a glowing neon logo with hexagon mark and "VANTAGE" text, a non-glowing yellow unit tag plate with barcode, yellow/black hazard stripes for the ram plate and rear step, and an LED display board for the rear face showing warning text — sticking to Latin characters since SVG text rendering may lack CJK font support.

I'm also planning a tinted windscreen with diagonal reflections and HUD text, a dark grille mesh with cyan accent lines, a gauge texture for the cannon tank labeled "BAR", a glowing headlight slit, and a wheel hub texture with a logo-stamped rim.

For the body I'm adding stenciled "CROWD CONTROL" door text with a yellow stripe on a transparent background, keeping it non-glowing, and skipping interior cab details and any tank water decals since they're not essential.

Instead I'm giving the rear a water-level sight window as a vertical blue glow strip with tick marks, which rounds out the texture set nicely to about ten total.

Now I'm sketching the paint materials: a livery hull paint, gunmetal paneling for the dark metal, rubbery noise texture for tires, plus iron and steel finishes for the chassis and cannon, with the cannon getting a blued-steel look and yellow banding along its barrel sweep.

For the banding I'm writing a color function that checks the surface position against band intervals to decide between yellow and steel. Then I move on to designing the water cannon turret itself -- the ring base and drum on the rear deck, an angular housing with armor plating and a glowing sensor lens, and the pitch cradle arms that will hold the barrel.

Now I'm shaping the barrel: a tapered sweep running from the breech near the cradle out to the nozzle, with radius values narrowing then flaring at the tip, and I'm sketching a lathe profile for the nozzle itself, outlining how the contour steps outward and back to form a flared lip without self-intersecting.

I also want to add a glowing cyan ring at the nozzle mouth, a pulsing blue "charged water" stripe along the barrel, and pressure hoses with ribbed segments sweeping from the rear tank to the turret.

For the cab, I'll add a camera sensor pod, warning beacon, roll bar roof rack, and an LRAD acoustic dish array mounted on the roof — but offset to either side at x ±0.7 so it clears the barrel's forward sweep path rather than sitting dead center.

Now I'm laying out the rest of the roof hardware: a light bar up front, LRAD dishes offset sideways, a centered camera dome that clears the barrel's height, plus rear-corner beacons and antennas. For the body I'm adding roof equipment rails, vents, hatch panels, a fire extinguisher mount, a torus-shaped safety rail ring around the turret, and a water tank fill cap with level gauge. On the cab sides I'm placing large mirror/camera pods, step bars, and door handles.

I'm adding wire mesh rods over the side windows, box-shaped fender arches over each wheel, mudflaps behind the rear wheels, underbody fuel tank boxes and a skid plate, and rod axles connecting the wheels plus a driveshaft -- checking that the axle height sits low enough to peek out from under the hull without clipping. For the wheels I'm building tire cylinders with sidewall rings and tread blocks, trying to keep per-wheel part counts merged down so the total part budget stays within limits while still hitting a reasonable triangle count.

Now I'm detailing the rims with a dark steel disc, beadlock ring with hex nuts, a hub texture plane, and a thin glowing cyan torus around the rim edge to give the wheels a neon cyberpunk look, positioning everything relative to the tire's outer face offset.

I'm setting up helper functions inside the build closure, like a shorthand `bx` for creating boxes attached to the chassis joint, so I can quickly place and orient each part without repeating boilerplate.

Defining Fill and V3 types...

Still defining material palettes...

Now I'm setting up the hull extrusion using the outline points at the hull surface, making sure the type annotations for the outline array are correct so numeric pairs aren't mismatched.

Then I'm working out the rear roof deck details at y=2.62—adding a raised armor rim frame around the perimeter with four low boxes, plus a turret ring pedestal positioned toward the back.

Still adding roof fixtures...

I'm also adding a rear light bar with alternating neon segments, sight tubes, a hazard-textured bumper step, tow hitch, red tail lamps, corner exhaust stacks, and a license plate, before moving to the front nose face and textured grille.

Still placing front details...

I'll keep the box with a front plane for the hazard texture to avoid stretching. For skirts, I'm adding dark side skirt boxes with cyan underglow between the wheel positions, and checking that fender flares properly cover the wheels where they'd otherwise intersect the hull wall.

Approximating the fender arch with a series of small rotated boxes placed around the wheel's top curve instead of trying to fight cylinder geometry parameters.

That confirms box depth of 0.31, with the fender region over the wheels fitting fine within the body width. Now I'm working out side details for the cab doors—placing the door panel at the hull side plane, splitting it into window glass area, lower dark armor plating with a handle, and a frame box positioned at the joint location.

For the door, I'll keep it simple with a darkened glass box, mesh bars across the window, handle, and hinge pins on the chassis, using the livery paint on the outer frame so the diagonal pattern continues seamlessly. Then I'm adding a neon logo plane on the rear flank, ribbed armor strips along the lower rear body (skipping the logo zone), and a cyan running strip broken into segments around the wheels.

Now I'm continuing the lighting with a continuous glowing cyan strip above the wheel arches and a magenta underglow box tucked beneath the hull between the wheels for a low-angle lighting effect. I'm also adding step bar rails near the cab with rubber plates, mirror arms with glowing camera-lens housings, a door-mounted "RSV-07" tag plane parented to the door bone, a whip antenna on the rear cab roof corner, and starting on the underbody axle rods.

Then I'm fleshing out the underbody with dark steel axles spanning the width, three differential pumpkins along the centerline, a driveshaft rod, leaf springs, a skid plate, fuel tank cylinders, and an exhaust pipe, keeping the gap between hull and ground modest and visible. For the cab roof I'm building a light bar with a base rail box and alternating cyan/magenta glowing segments, dark end caps with red/blue accents, a thin glowing lens strip on the front face, plus a grille light bar and rooftop spotlight.

I'm adding LRAD speaker units on pedestal cylinders with lathe-profile dishes aimed forward-up, each with a small glowing cyan emitter disc at center, along with a camera dome and sensor mast on the roof. Then I move to turret details, starting with a steel torus ring mounted around the turret base.

Continuing with turret geometry...

Still working out geometry...

Adding the rear shroud box with hose connectors behind the turret, then setting up the pitching parts like the breech block and barrel sweep geometry.

Now I'm placing the yellow collar bands along the barrel, mounting pressure gauges on the cheeks, adding trunnion cylinders at the pivot points, building the muzzle nozzle with its glowing mouth ring, and topping it off with a camera sensor pod featuring a cyan glowing lens.

For orienting each torus ring along the hose path, I need to rotate the ring's local Z-axis by 90° around X so it aligns with the tangent direction at each sample point. I'll use the along-path iterator to place rings every so often, inheriting bone weighting from whichever joint is nearest along that segment.

Since hoses run from the deck to the rotating turret yaw, they should be weighted to the yaw bone explicitly rather than relying on nearest-joint inference, since explicit bone assignment always takes priority. I'll simplify by skipping dense ring segments and just using the along-path sweep, then layer in neon accents: cyan glow lines on the turret cheeks, yellow hazard stripes, and a blue glow for the water-charge indicator.

Adding a thin glowing cyan-blue strip along the top of the barrel, positioned where the taper narrows toward the muzzle, then considering whether to add a rack of translucent riot shields mounted along the rear body sides for extra detail.

Working out exact placement: logo centered around z -0.8 to -0.1, with three riot shields fitting into the z -3.12 to -1.67 range, spaced to clear the wheel arch and hull corner, each shield outlined as a rounded rectangle with a visor window extruded along the body.

I'm skipping the rear ladder detail and estimating the total part count should land around 250-350, which feels reasonable. Now I'm adding a windscreen mesh guard made of angled rods positioned along the glass's slope, offset slightly outward using the surface normal to give it an armored look.

Still placing rods and bars...

I'm also positioning the actual windscreen glass plane itself, offsetting it slightly above the hull surface to account for bevel recesses along the sloped cab edges so it sits correctly without clipping into the hull.

I'm sketching out remaining body details next: side window glass overlay, the hood slope between the nose and cab with vent details, plus mirrors and exhaust, and I'm designing a neon hexagonal "VANTAGE" logo graphic with cyan and magenta accents for the vehicle livery.

Writing SVG code...

Writing more SVG assets...

Adding grille and rim designs...

I'm planning the water level glass tube, gauge textures from the clockwork kit, flat glowing discs for the sensor lens and headlights, a red tail lamp glow, and a roof stencil plane with "RSV-07" lettering oriented upward facing front.

Now I'm working out roof deck layout: positioning the turret, fitting the stencil plane into the gap between the turret and cab, and placing rear vent hatches on either side without overlapping the stencil or turret.

Adding beacon placement next: cylinder bases with yellow glow domes and hinge joints positioned at either side, plus a rear bumper step with a hazard-striped plane on the back face.

Now I'm positioning the rear lighting details - vertical red tail lamps, an alternating neon light bar across the back, and a rear LED display board, working out the orientation vectors so the display's local axes align correctly with the viewer's perspective.

Working out LED board sizing against the tube positions, settling on 1.7×0.62 centered at y 1.7. Now placing vertical exhaust stacks at the rear corners, checking they clear the shield geometry near the hull edges.

I'm positioning the stacks behind the cab with thin sweeps and heat shield caps, verifying they sit correctly against the rear body geometry without clashing with the door window or logo placement. Moving on to roof rails and mirror arm positions next.

Now I'm adding a rear camera housing with glass and a glowing lens, plus front bumper details like tow hooks, winch, and spotlight pods with cyan glow lamps on the push bar. I'm also naming door joints and setting up the cannon barrel as a tapered sweep along a pitch-controlled path.

Still shaping the nozzle and blue accent rings...

Checking clearance for the nozzle tip and torus barrel against the cheek geometry, everything stays below the overhead limit. I'm defining the pitch joint rotation axis and positioning the barrel parts on that bone, then placing a gauge plane on the outward face of the left cheek.

I'm setting up the circle geometry for the gauge display so the texture fills the disc properly, then adding the bezel cylinder. Now I'm sketching out the joint structure, mirroring loops for symmetric parts, and tallying a rough part count across the hull, windows, rods, nose, bumper, and wheel assemblies.

Setting up TypeScript imports...

Defining helper geometry functions...

Writing tread geometry generator...

Still assembling wheel geometry...

Writing ring-merge helper function...

Writing fender geometry helper...

Now I'm laying out the actual coordinates: front wheels at z=2.1, mid at z=0, rear at z=-2.1, with the hull nose at z=3.3 and bumper slightly ahead at 3.45. I'm checking that the rear body, wheel positions, and fender shields don't overlap along the z-axis.

I'm positioning the cab door relative to the front wheel arch, making sure the door panel, window glass, and hinge sit cleanly above the arch without clipping. I'm defining the door as a lower panel, an upper frame, and an inset window piece with specific dimensions and placement.

Still placing door hardware...

Now I'm defining the livery paint function, using noise for dirt and a diagonal cutoff based on z-position to split the hull into lower and upper color bands.

I'm checking texel density against the hull's surface area — with roughly 150 m² painted and 2048² texture resolution, seams around 2.5mm thick would fall below a single texel's resolution at ~7mm/texel, so they might not render clearly.

Since the panelled approach won't resolve fine seams reliably, I'll implement wider 8mm-wide seam lines myself directly in the livery paint logic, computing a UV coordinate from surface normal and position, then measuring distance to the nearest periodic seam boundary and marking it as a seam if within ~6mm (12mm total width). I'll skip the panelled system for livery and handle hull-side panel splits (like doors) the same way, switching axes depending on whether the surface normal points mostly vertical or horizontal. I also want to cut down the total painted area to ease texel budget constraints.

Now I'm defining the paint set: plated iron with light tarnish and rivets for small parts, steel and blued metal variants, a dark rubber mottle texture, and a cannon paint that draws yellow hazard bands near the muzzle and breech with blued metal elsewhere, nesting one paint call inside another. I'm setting up the build function and export metadata before writing the main construction code.

Setting up skeleton joints...

Adding axle hub caps, fender rings tied to the chassis bone, and mudflaps positioned behind the rear and mid wheels...

Still placing axle rods, differential spheres, leaf springs, and a dark skid plate underneath with a thin neon glow strip...

I'll split the side strips into two segments per side, avoiding the wheel zones, placed at x ±1.0 with centers around z 1.05 and -1.05, plus adding a center strip under the nose where it crosses.

Simplifying to just the one strip segment on the door body, and maybe a short front segment near the hull's forward taper -- checking how far the side panel extends in z at that height to keep the strip within the body outline.

Now working through the front-end geometry: the face angle near the headlight area, plus placement for the grille plane and hull bevel, then sketching the neon headlight boxes positioned near the front corners.

I'm positioning the cyan DRL strip along the nose's top edge, adding brow guards above the headlights, and setting up the push bumper's base plate dimensions.

I'm working out the hazard plane geometry and side wedge shapes for the bumper corners, using rotated boxes to approximate the angled wedges since no frustum helper exists.

For the push bars, I'm placing angled vertical tubes near the grille that run from the bumper top up to a crossbar near the hood, forming a slanted mesh with thin rods, and adding a cyan neon strip mounted just in front of the crossbar.

Now I'm adding yellow tow hook shackle plates near the bumper corners, plus small cylindrical spotlight pods with neon white faces positioned at the bumper top edges. Then I'm working out the hood vent louvre placement, calculating the y-coordinate along the sloped hood surface so the vent blocks sit flush against the angled hood panel.

Adding rear light bar segments...

Shaping the dish outline so the lathed profile curves outward and up without self-intersecting, keeping the concave face pointed toward the emitter axis, then adding a glow disc for the emitter.

Now I'm adding the emitter cylinder aligned along the dish axis with a cyan neon glow wrapper, plus a pedestal and offset dish mount. I'm also sketching a camera dome with a half-sphere housing and cyan lens glow, and placing whip antennas near the cab while skipping the beacon area.

Working out antenna rod placement at the rear corners using a tapered spike shape with a small ball tip, checking it clears the cab roof, light bar, and LRAD positions without overlapping.

I notice the LRAD dish at x .7 slightly overlaps nearby elements, so I'm nudging it inward to x ±0.62 for clearance. The mirrors are already handled, and now I'm thinking through where to add rib detailing on the lower rear body, considering vertical ribs near the corners, a vent panel, fill cap, and hose reel placement along the side.

Between the mid and rear wheel arches there's a gap I'm filling with a hatch plate carrying two yellow-capped Storz hose couplings and chains on both sides. I'm also laying out three shield panels along the rear flank with set widths and heights, mounted via brackets rising from the hull.

For the shields I'm giving them dark glass tint with a neon cyan glow strip along the top and bottom edges rather than the full outline. For the rear, I'm adding a plated bumper step, a hazard-stripe plane, and a simple tow ball hitch, while skipping the license plate and rear window since they don't apply to this body style.

Now I'm working out exhaust stack placement: vertical pipe rods with clamp brackets, starting above the fender arch at y 1.35 so they clear the wheel wells, running up to y 3.0, with a heat shield cylinder and cap at the top.

For beacon lights I'm splitting into two bones per side — a static chassis base with the glow dome, and a separate spinning bone holding the dark reflector box, so only the dome emits light while the reflector rotates independently. I'm skipping a rear satellite dish for now but considering double rear doors with seam lines and handles, a small sight-glass water window on the flank, and placing the flank neon hex logo plane at the right position and size to cover that side region.

I'm also checking logo placement against roof height limits and resolving a collision with the existing side strip — the strip crosses through the lower part of the logo, so I need to break it into separate segments that route around the logo zone instead of running straight through. For the "CROWD SUPPRESSION UNIT" text, I'm deciding to place it on the cab door rather than near the rear shields to avoid clutter, then moving on to work out the overall livery.

Adjusting the dark backing panel and neon frame dimensions so the logo lightbox fits cleanly within the roofline without exceeding it, then preparing to write out the full vehicle code in detail.

I'm reviewing the available API primitives — sweep, lathe, extrude, frustumBox, spike, and along — to decide how to build the hose geometry, sketching out a catmull path for a curved rubber hose using sweep with a small radius and hexagonal cross-section.

For the along rings along the hose, I'm placing small torus clamps at intervals, rotating each to align with the path tangent using the frame's quaternion, confirming that passing the path frame directly as the `at` option works correctly. I'm also noting that pitch rotation happens around X, while yaw should apply to all turret parts except the barrel group.

Now I'm defining the yaw and pitch joints with their positions and hinge directions, then building a mounting ring with a bolt circle made of small cylinders merged into one geometry, and sketching out a lathe-based drum base for the turret.

Still shaping the turret cheeks...

Now I'm adding the rear shroud block and vent slats, plus a slanted top hatch cover, and thinking through how the pitch bone's rotation affects the attached bar geometry.

I'm placing the breech block between the receiver cheeks and working out barrel length and positioning so the breech cap sits just behind it near the rear shroud, accepting the minor collision risk since it won't be visually obvious.

Now I'm positioning the trunnions symmetrically outside the cheeks with outward-facing knobs, then placing a gauge dial on the left cheek offset from the trunnion so they don't overlap visually.

I'm checking the gauge against the sloped cheek outline to make sure it stays within the panel boundary, nudging its vertical position slightly lower to clear the edge.

Now I'm adding yellow torus collars around the barrel at specific axial positions, sizing the ring and tube radii to match the barrel's taper.

I'm also adding a mid-barrel water-jacket cylinder with a glow strip, a camera pod box on top with a forward-facing lens disc, and starting to lay out the nozzle geometry at the barrel's front end.

I'm placing a small beacon bar on the rear shroud, deciding to skip a "HYDRA" text decal, and now positioning a rear-roof stencil plane reading "RSV-07" sized to fit the body's upper rear section.

Working out the orientation math for that plane—figuring out which way "right" points relative to the top-down view so the stencil text reads correctly.

Orientation checks out. I'm now moving to the roof stencil detail in yellow, tagging the door plane, and starting the rim texture SVG as a circular viewBox element.

Still writing rim graphics...

Fill type accepts a string or Paint, which works fine for the glow color. I'm checking the part signature takes geometry, color, and options, then returning the final root, while double-checking the wheel geometry so the tread blocks sit properly against the tire radius without clipping below the ground plane.

Checking proportions: tread ring radius at 0.52-0.53 keeps block overhang within the height tolerance, and overall turret/antenna height stacks correctly at 3.6m. Writing helper function for ring geometry...

Writing the build function scaffold...

Writing livery paint logic...

Simplifying the seam detection with a fractional distance helper, then darkening the color near seams and blending in grime for a weathered panel look.

Checking the plane/decal helper works with circle geometry for the rim hub texture, and verifying the glow logic skips textured "paint" parts correctly. I'm also setting up hinge joints for the beacon attachment points.
